text:
- [RCTS.1.2.21] **`expect.tamper`** (optional, `runtime_error`,
  `replay_determinism` and `runtime_fact_count` only) — an edit a harness must make to the compiled
  artefact before the runtime loads it. It is a string, an object of exactly one member from a closed set, or a
  list of such objects.

  A string names one byte, whose lowest bit a harness must flip, leaving the
  stored `dsc_sha256` as the compiler wrote it ([RDSC.3.6]):

  - `dsc_sha256`: the first byte of the header's `dsc_sha256`;
  - `last_byte`: the artefact's last byte.

  An object names one structural edit. A harness must make it and then
  recompute `dsc_sha256` over the edited artefact as [RDSC.3.6] states, so
  that a refusal at load is the edit's and not the hash's. The hash it
  recomputes is the 32-byte field 7 of the first `DscHeader` atom that a walk
  of the artefact's frames ([RFCS.19.1]) reaches from its first byte. Where
  the walk reaches none, or that atom's body does not walk to such a field,
  there is no hash to recompute, and a harness must hand the runtime the
  artefact as the edit left it:

  - `truncate_tail`, an integer N greater than 0 and less than the artefact's
    length: its last N bytes are removed ([RDSC.9.7]);
  - `truncate_to`, an integer N of at least 0 and less than the artefact's
    length: it keeps its first N bytes, so N = 0 leaves it empty
    ([RDSC.11.1]);
  - `bad_wire_type`, an atom's field number F: the first byte of the body of
    the first atom numbered F, which begins a field's key, gets wire type 7
    ([RDSC.9.5]);
  - `drop_schema_group`, a schema name S: the atoms of S's schema group, from
    its lifecycle atom through its `SchemaDef`, are removed ([RDSC.8.1],
    [RDSC.8.7]);
  - `drop_terminal_parent`, a rule name R: the `BetaNode` whose id the
    `TerminalNode` realizing R carries as `parent_beta_id` is removed
    ([RDSC.11.1]);
  - `drop_call_operand`, a rule name R: in the one `TerminalNode` realizing
    R, the first action that is an `ACTION_CALL` whose `expr` is a `call`
    loses the last of that call's `args` ([RDSC.4a.9.3]). The artefact is
    not refused at load for it, so the fault a fixture names comes from one
    of its steps.

  Four more each make one of [RDSC.11.3]'s load refusals, in the one
  `TerminalNode` realizing a rule R:

  - `drop_action_expr`, a rule name R: the first action of kind `ACTION_CALL`
    loses its `expr`;
  - `clear_action_expr`, a rule name R: that action's `expr` is replaced by an
    `Expr` with no field, so no member of its `kind` is set;
  - `drop_assign_expr`, a rule name R: the first `SlotAssign` of the first
    action of kind `ACTION_ASSERT` or `ACTION_LOGICAL_ASSERT` loses its
    `expr`;
  - `nest_action_expr`, an object of exactly two members, `rule`, a rule name
    R, and `levels`, an integer N of at least 1: the `expr` E of the first
    action of kind `ACTION_CALL` is replaced by an `Expr` whose `unop` is a
    `not` of operand E, N times over, so every `Expr` in E sits N deeper.

  Two more each set the `op` of one `CallExpr` to N, in the one
  `TerminalNode` realizing a rule R, so that the op stands at one of
  [RDSC.4a.9.3]'s two sites. Each is an object of exactly two members,
  `rule`, a rule name R, and `op`, an integer N of at least 0. A harness
  must write N as the call's `op`, its field 3, after the call's other
  fields, and drop the one it had:

  - `set_action_op`: the call that is the `expr` of the first action of
    kind `ACTION_CALL` whose `expr` is a `call`, so N stands as an action's
    `expr`;
  - `set_assign_op`: the call that is the `expr` of the first `SlotAssign`
    of the first action of kind `ACTION_ASSERT` or `ACTION_LOGICAL_ASSERT`,
    so N stands inside an expression.

  For these two, an `expr` that is no `call`, or a call with no `op`
  written, is no site.

  Two more each make the `DscHeader`'s `capabilities` list one [RBND.1.3]
  refuses at load. A harness must edit the list in place, written packed and
  every entry one varint byte, so no length moves:

  - `duplicate_capability`, an integer I of at least 0: entry I + 1 takes
    entry I's value, so one capability appears twice;
  - `swap_capabilities`, an integer I of at least 0: entries I and I + 1
    swap, so the list is not ascending.

  For these two, a list with no entry I + 1, with an entry wider than one
  byte, or not written packed is no site.

  One more sets one field of one atom, as no compiler writes it, so that a
  body refusal of [RDSC.4a.3], [RDSC.4a.6], [RDSC.4a.6.1], [RDSC.4a.9.1] or
  [RDSC.9.10] can be a fixture:

  - `set_field`, an object of exactly three members: either `node`, an
    integer N of at least 1, or `atom`, an array of two integers, an atom
    number F of at least 1 and an occurrence index I of at least 0; `path`,
    an array of integers, a field number of at least 1 and then any number
    of pairs of an occurrence index of at least 0 and a field number; and
    `value`, an integer of at least 0, a string, an object of exactly one
    member, `f64`, whose value is a string of 16 lowercase hexadecimal
    digits, or `null`.
    With `node`, the atom is the one `AlphaNode`, `BetaNode` or
    `TerminalNode` whose `node_id` is N; with `atom`, it is occurrence I,
    counted from 0, of the atoms numbered F, in the artefact's order. In
    that atom, each pair of a field number and an index selects that
    occurrence, counted from 0, of that length-delimited field of the
    message reached so far, and the path's last field number names a field
    of the last message reached. A harness must remove every occurrence of
    that field and then, unless `value` is `null`, write it once after that
    message's other fields: an integer as a varint; an `f64` as the 64 bits
    its digits spell, most significant first, with wire type 1 and the
    eight octets least significant first, as a `double` is written; and a
    string as its UTF-8 octets, length-delimited, so `""` also writes an
    empty message. A harness must re-frame every message on the path, and
    the atom.

  For `set_field`, no node or two nodes with the id N, fewer than I + 1
  atoms numbered F, an occurrence the message does not carry, a selected
  field that is not length-delimited, or `null` for a field the message does
  not carry is no site.

  Two more remove or add whole frames, so that [RDSC.11.1]'s rows for an
  artefact that is not an atom container, and its framing rows, can be
  fixtures. Each counts the artefact's atoms from 0, by a walk of its frames
  from its first byte:

  - `drop_atom`, an integer K of at least 0: atom K's frame is removed, so
    K = 0 removes the `DscHeader`;
  - `insert_bytes`, an object of exactly two members: `at`, an integer K of
    at least 0, and `hex`, a string of an even number, at least two, of
    lowercase hexadecimal digits. The octets `hex` spells, two digits to an
    octet, most significant digit first, are inserted before atom K, or
    after the last atom when K is the number of atoms. They need not make a
    frame, and a fixture's scenario says what they are.

  For `drop_atom`, a K that is not less than the number of atoms the walk
  reaches is no site. For `insert_bytes`, a K greater than that number is
  no site, and so is a walk that stops before the artefact's end.

  A list names two or more of the objects above, none of them
  `drop_call_operand`, so that one artefact can carry two defects and a
  fixture can pin which of them a loader refuses first ([RDSC.9.5],
  [RDSC.8.7]). A harness must make the edits in the list's order, each to
  the artefact the ones before it left, and then recompute `dsc_sha256` once,
  over the result, as [RDSC.3.6] states. Each edit must have a site in the
  artefact it is made to.

  On a `replay_determinism` fixture, `tamper` must be `drop_call_operand`,
  and a harness must give the edited artefact to both the engine that
  records and the engine that replays. The run must halt the engine ([NCBK.2.9]), and a harness must fail a fixture
  whose run does not; the step during which it halts is the run's outcome
  ([RCTS.1.2.28]). The replay must reach the end of the recording
  ([RFCS.6.7]) and leave the replaying engine halted by the fault that halted
  the recording one. A harness must not read the replaying engine's working
  memory: on a halted engine it is undefined ([LERR.1.4.7]) and the read is
  refused ([NCBK.2.9]).

  On a `runtime_fact_count` fixture, `tamper` must be an object other than
  `drop_call_operand`, or a list, so that a run on an edited artefact that
  must raise nothing can be a fixture ([RCTS.1.2.31]). A string's artefact is
  refused at load for its hash, and `drop_call_operand`'s fault is a step's,
  which that kind does not observe. A harness must make the edit before
  `add_compiled_code`'s, and must fail the fixture when the runtime refuses
  the edited artefact at load.

  A harness must fail a fixture whose `tamper` names no member of the set,
  gives a member an argument of another type, or has no site in the
  artefact. It must fail a list of fewer than two members, or one holding a
  string, a list or `drop_call_operand`. It must fail a `replay_determinism`
  fixture whose `tamper` is anything but `drop_call_operand`, a
  `runtime_fact_count` fixture whose `tamper` is a string or
  `drop_call_operand`, and a fixture of any other `expect.kind` that carries
  the field. The set grows only by a
  change to this clause.
